The accepted 'dense 0.79-0.85 > TF-IDF 0.71-0.74' claim is a pair-set mismatch + self-pair artifact. For citation-heritage views, use the citation graph / a full-dimensional citation representation; dense is justified only as a text-only proxy when citations are unavailable. Resolves cross-lane contradiction in favour of the evaluation lane's retraction.

critical_findings.citation_heritage_text_only_proxy_v36: CONFIRMED (v36, run 38051603155): for corpora WITHOUT a citation graph, dense multilingual-e5 (center-projected PCA-64) is a materially better text-only citation-heritage proxy than any TF-IDF text-only baseline. Identical matched self-pair-free ORIG (606/834): dense_cp64 0.7189 vs best text-only regeste_full_text_hybrid_0.7 0.5866 (margin +0.1324, CI +0.0925..+0.1709); DIRECT hard-matched (5255/6008): 0.6924 vs 0.5616 (+0.1308). full_text_tfidf_light (used in the original non-comparable claim) is NOT the strongest text-only rep (0.5308; regeste_tfidf is the weakest at 0.4850, below chance). This scopes the dense complementary role to the no-graph fallback and does not affect the v35 result that the citation graph beats dense on DIRECT and is an oracle on SHARED.
